questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Boys and the Frogs'?
choices: Think whether your fun may make someone else unhappy
Throwing stones is good exercise for growing boys
Frogs are braver animals than most people think
Never play near a pond or you may fall into it
questions.evidence: Always stop to think whether your fun may not be the cause of another's unhappiness.

questions.q: In 'The Crow and the Pitcher', how did the Crow get the water?
choices: He dropped pebbles in until the water rose
He tipped the pitcher over with his strong beak
He broke the pitcher open with a heavy stone
He waited beside it until the rain filled it
questions.evidence: he dropped them into the pitcher one by one

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Crow and the Pitcher'?
choices: Using our wits well may help us out of trouble
Always carry water with you on a hot day
Crows are greedy birds that waste their water
Do not attempt the impossible, or you will fail
questions.evidence: In a pinch a good use of our wits may help us out.

questions.q: In 'The Ants and the Grasshopper', why did the Grasshopper have no food for winter?
choices: He was busy making music all summer
The Ants had taken all his food away
His food got wet and rotted in the rain
He gave all of it away to his friends
questions.evidence: I was so busy making music that before I knew it the summer was gone.

questions.q: In 'The Ass Carrying the Image', why did the Ass stop and bray?
choices: He thought the people were honoring him
He was tired and hungry after the long walk
He was scared of the large crowd in the street
His load was far too heavy for him to carry
questions.evidence: the Ass thought the honor was being paid to himself

questions.q: In 'A Raven and a Swan', why did the Raven move to the lakes and marshes?
choices: He hoped his feathers would turn white
He wanted to catch fish like the Swan did
His home in the woods had burned down
The Swan had invited him to come and stay
questions.evidence: his feathers would turn white like the Swan's

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'A Raven and a Swan'?
choices: A change of habits will not alter nature
Swimming every day will make you strong
Eat the same food as those you admire
Black feathers are better than white ones
questions.evidence: A change of habits will not alter nature.

questions.q: In 'The Two Goats', why did both Goats fall into the torrent?
choices: Their pride would not let either one give way
The log broke under them in the middle
A strong storm blew them off the bridge
They slipped on the wet rocks by the stream
questions.evidence: Their pride would not permit either to stand aside for the other.
